statusHistory.note: Ad-hoc war-room slate item (Amsterdam: 'record shop that's a club-culture institution'). ADDRESS RESOLVED: current, correct address is Spuistraat 110, 1012 VA Amsterdam — confirmed on Rush Hour's own contact page (rushhour.nl/contact) and cross-checked against Waze, Corner, and findglocal listings, all agreeing on 110. Resident Advisor's March 2022 relocation piece (ra.co/news/76974) explains the '116' figure still floating around some directories (e.g. Yelp, which is stale): Rush Hour moved on the weekend of 21 March 2022 from its prior spot — occupied roughly six years, since ~2016 — to Spuistraat 110, described by cofounder Antal as 'just three doors down from the old spot,' gaining a two-floor space (ground-floor shop + basement used at peak times/for in-stores). So 116 was a real former address, not a typo, but it is now superseded; 110 is correct and current as of this research (Sept 2026) and should be used everywhere. History verified via rushhour.nl/about-rush-hour-music: founded late 1997 by Antal and partners as a mail-order/import shop for obscure house and techno; distribution arm added 1999; in-house label launched just before 2000; monthly residency at Paradiso from 1998 onward, later expanding to Trouw, OT301, and Rush Hour nights abroad (London, Paris, New York, Tokyo, Berlin). Club-culture/DJ-scene weight corroborated by DJ Mag's longread and The Vinyl Factory: artists associated with the label/shop include Hunee, Young Marco, Interstellar Funk, Tom Trago, Awanto 3, and San Proper (who has a Rush Hour tattoo); the label's Soichi Terada compilation is credited with reviving his career, and it has also released Ryuichi Sakamoto and Ron Trent. This is a genuine club-culture/DJ-culture institution, not generic retail — hence the stefan byline per operator instruction rather than a shopping-beat persona. DATED 2026 IN-STORE VERIFIED, NOT JUST RESTATED: checked rushhour.nl/events directly (not a secondary aggregator) and found a real, specific, currently-listed in-store — 'Lex Records presents: Lord Jah-Monte Ogbon & Vayda — Lex Live Instore,' Thursday 3 September 2026, in the Rush Hour Basement. Also on the same official page: a Used Record Sale on 14 October 2026, and a Rush Hour x Lofi off-site ADE '26 event on 24 October 2026 (not an in-store, excluded from the dated hook for that reason). The 3 September in-store is the one used in the body copy since it is an actual in-house event matching the BACKLOG's 'in-store' framing. IMAGE CHECK: searched Wikimedia Commons directly (title search and MediaSearch for 'Rush Hour Spuistraat Amsterdam' and variants) and found zero results — confirming the BACKLOG note that no rights-clear Commons image exists for this venue. heroImage left null. Illustration brief for near-illustrator: a two-level Amsterdam canal-house record shop interior on Spuistraat, ground floor with a 'living room feel' (per RA's description of the 2022 redesign) — crates of house/techno vinyl, a listening station, warm wood and daylight from tall canal-house windows up front, with a hint of a basement stair leading down to a small in-store performance space; avoid generic 'cool record shop' clichés and lean into the specific two-floor, canal-house-into-basement-venue layout that's actually distinctive here. Coordinates are a manual approximation for Spuistraat 110 in Amsterdam Centrum (confidence 0.5); a precise geocode lookup is still owed before this leaves draft.
